title: PostgreSQL with Docker
idea: Docker runs PostgreSQL in a container, an isolated process, on your laptop. A published port lets your app reach it; a volume keeps the data.
points: `docker run -d` starts the `postgres:18` image as a container in the background.
`POSTGRES_PASSWORD` is required. `POSTGRES_DB` names the database created on first start.
`-p 127.0.0.1:5432:5432` publishes the container's port on your machine only.
`-v url-shortener-data:/var/lib/postgresql` keeps the data when the container is removed.

hero.title: A database that outlives its container

steps.caption: Your app has a `DATABASE_URL`, but no database is running yet.
`docker run` starts the container and creates the volume. Postgres sets up an empty database.
The published port forwards `localhost:5432` into the container. The app connects.
Postgres writes its files to the volume, not to the container itself.
`docker rm -f` removes the container. The named volume stays.
A new `docker run` with the same `-v` finds the data and leaves it untouched.

code.title: Start Postgres
code.caption: The same recipe as chapter 5, with this project's names. Not run here: it needs Docker.

walk.text: Name the container, so later commands can refer to it.
Set the superuser password. It is required; `demo-password` is a demo value.
Create a database called `shortener` on first start.
Mount the named volume where Postgres 18 keeps its data.
Publish container port 5432 on host port 5432, reachable from this machine only.
Run in the background (`-d`) from the `postgres:18` image.
`docker ps` lists running containers. `stop` and `start` halt and restart the same one.

code.title: .env file
code.caption: Save this as `.env` in the project root. `DATABASE_URL` is the address your app connects to; the next lesson reads it part by part. The password is a demo value.

pitfalls: `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` and `POSTGRES_DB` apply only on first start with an empty volume.
Postgres 18 images mount `/var/lib/postgresql`; older ones used `/var/lib/postgresql/data`.
If port 5432 is taken, use `-p 127.0.0.1:5433:5432` and change the port in `DATABASE_URL`.

quiz.q: After `docker rm -f` and a new `docker run` with the same `-v`, what happens to the rows?
options: They are gone with the container
Docker restores them from the image
Postgres asks you to recreate them
quiz.why: A named volume lives outside the container, and removing the container keeps it. The new container finds the data and leaves it untouched.

takeaway: Publish the port to connect; mount a volume to keep the data.
